C-AGT-1.c.title: Webhooks refuse over-size bodies with 413
C-AGT-1.c.approach: Root cause: `RequestBodyBufferMiddleware(MAX_API_BODY_BYTES)` (`src/Server/Server.php:241`) does not refuse an over-limit body; it swaps in an empty body and calls `$next`. `HookWebhooks::handle()` then splices `PromptFence::escape('')` (`src/Server/Http/HookWebhooks.php:130-133`) and spawns a billed turn (:136). Fix: before the splice, answer `413 payload_too_large` when `Content-Length` > `ServerConfig::MAX_API_BODY_BYTES`, or when a body was declared (`Content-Length` > 0 or `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`) and the buffered body is `''`. `$run` is never invoked on that path. Correct the :127-129 docblock and document the 413 in `docs/SERVER.md`.
C-AGT-1.c.tests: modify `candy-code/tests/Server/HookWebhooksTest.php` (`Content-Length: 70000` with an empty body → 413, `$run` never called); create `candy-code/tests/Server/HookWebhooksBodyCapStackTest.php` (posts 70 KiB through the real middleware stack → 413)
C-AGT-1.c.docs/guards: `docs/SERVER.md` row; `ServerProtocolDocumentationDriftTest` stays green (the endpoint table wording only)
C-AGT-1.c.risks: real GitHub push payloads over 64 KiB now get a loud 413 instead of a silent empty run. A per-hook body cap is out of scope (noted for C-AGT-5.d).

C-AGT-5.a.approach:

- Turns run forked, so the tool writes PERSISTED rows only; the file under its lock is the channel, and hosts reload by digest. It builds `ScheduleRegistry::loadDefault($context->root)` from `ToolBuildContext::$root`, so no LaunchContext/Bootstrap threading is needed.

- Mode is no looser than the session's and never bypass-class (the C-AGT-7.a ceiling); the default is the `dont-ask` floor.
- At most N model-created rows per root; the cadence floor comes from `Schedule`.
- A shared `Background\ScheduleFactory` holds the validation that `/schedules add` (5.b) reuses.
- Pin `Schedule` in `Runtime::WRITE_CAPABLE_TOOL_NAMES` (:704).

C-AGT-5.c.title: Heartbeat schedule kind
C-AGT-5.c.approach:
- A row gains `kind: "task"|"heartbeat"`. For a heartbeat, `ScheduleSpawner` appends "reply exactly HEARTBEAT_OK when nothing needs attention".
- When the daemon settles, Chat's `pumpBackgroundSessions()` suppresses the queued announcement turn for an `HEARTBEAT_OK` answer, and otherwise announces it and rings `terminalNotification()` (OSC 9).
- On serve the run stays an ordinary `bg.completed` row. Web push is C-WEB-5's job (LATE), so it is NOT a dependency.
- `/schedules add --heartbeat` and the tool's `kind` param pass it through.

C-AGT-5.d.title: Signed inbound webhooks + delivery dedupe
C-AGT-5.d.approach:
Each `webhooks` row gains an optional `signature: {scheme: "github-sha256"|"hmac-sha256", header?}` (`ServerConfig::webhooksValue()` ~:700-770).
- With a scheme, `HookWebhooks::handle()` verifies `sha256=<hex>` over the RAW body with the row's secret through `hash_equals`, in place of the `x-candy-code-hook` header, because GitHub cannot send custom headers.
- A per-hook LRU of delivery ids (`X-GitHub-Delivery`, or a configured `deliveryHeader`) answers a replay `200 {ok:true, duplicate:true}` without spawning.
- Failed signatures feed the same lockout limiter.
- A GitHub recipe goes in `docs/SERVER.md`.
C-AGT-5.d.tests: create `candy-code/tests/Server/HookWebhooksSignatureTest.php` (a valid GitHub signature runs; a bad one → 401 and counts toward lockout; a replayed delivery id spawns nothing); modify `candy-code/tests/Server/ServerConfigWebhooksTest.php` (`signature` parse and refusals)
C-AGT-5.d.risks: GitHub push payloads often exceed the 64 KiB global body cap (now a loud 413 from C-AGT-1.c). A per-route larger cap would be a separate server change.

C-AGT-6.a.title: `/commit` with a drafted message
C-AGT-6.a.approach:
`/commit [message]` is a builtin with a host body, so serve and web get it as `runsIn: server`.
- `CommitHostCommand` returns `CommandEffect::async`, which collects every changed path (`git status --porcelain -z`).
- With no message, it drafts the subject on the title backend through `CommitMessageWriter::request()`/`subjectFrom()`, falling back to `CommitMessageWriter::fallback()`.
- It commits through a new public `AutoCommitter::commitAll(string $subject)`: the hardened `commit()` path, recorded as kind `command`, so `/undo` can revert it.
- It replies with the sha, subject and file count. "Nothing to commit" is a plain reply.
- It is not read-only-safe: the default, so no roster edit.
- The Chat handler is one line through `runHostCommand`. The new spec file is per-command-disjoint.
C-AGT-6.a.tests: create `candy-code/tests/Host/Commands/CommitHostCommandTest.php` (temp repo: given message → commit and sha; no message → scripted title backend drafts `feat: …`; clean tree → reply, no commit; read-only window refused; `/undo` reverts it); modify `candy-code/tests/Workspace/AutoCommitterTest.php` (`commitAll`)

C-AGT-6.b.title: `/review` ranges (`A..B`, `A...B`, `@{u}`)
C-AGT-6.b.item: C-AGT-6 (sources: p2-miss: GIT-10 review scope parity, GIT-1-P1 fix (b))
C-AGT-6.b.approach:
`ContextMentions::diff()` (:234) learns ranges, through the same bounded `GitRunner` and safety flags:
- `A..B` → `git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color -M --patch A B`;
- `A...B` → `git diff --merge-base A B`, falling back to `merge-base` + `diff` on an old git.
- `isDiffRef()` and `ReviewCommand::refError()` re-admit `..`/`...` only in those two shapes. `refError()` pre-resolves each side.
- `cmd.review.hint` and `bad-ref` list the accepted forms again.
- Untracked files stay out, as documented.

C-AGT-7.a.title: Schedule hygiene: watch tick, bypass ceiling, run limit
C-AGT-7.a.approach:
- P2: `Chat::subscriptions()` arms the 2 s tick only when a row is enabled or a daemon is active (`src/Chat.php:18118-18128`), so a row hand-written after an empty launch never fires in that TUI. Add a slow 30 s watch tick, armed whenever the registry has a backing path (`ScheduleRegistry::isWatchable()`), that reloads by digest. C-AGT-4.e's mailbox drain reuses it.
- P3: `Schedule` coerces only unknown modes (:110), so a spelled `bypass-permissions` row runs unattended. Refuse bypass-class rows at load with a named note and skip the row, matching the webhook refusal (`ServerConfig.php:753`).
- P4: the docblock "no timeout anywhere" (:207) is false, because `spawnSession()` defaults to 3600 s. Correct it, and accept an optional row `timeoutSeconds` (bounded, at least 60) that `ScheduleSpawner` passes through. The default 3600 is documented. This is a session cap, not an LLM request timeout (E646).

C-EXT-1.a.title: CC hook entries: accept `statusMessage`/`async`, Claude exit-code dialect
C-EXT-1.a.approach:
- **Root cause.** `candy-code/src/Hooks/ClaudeSettingsHooks.php:98` has `ENTRY_KEYS = ['type','command','timeout']`, and `:247-255` refuses the whole launch on any other key. Claude Code writes `statusMessage` and `async` routinely. Separately, `ScriptHook.php:782-811` maps every exit code except 0/3/4 to DENY, so a CC hook that exits 1 blocks the call where Claude Code proceeds.
- **Fix.**
- The parser accepts `statusMessage`, mapped onto the native `description`, which `/hooks` shows.
- The parser accepts `async: true`. candy-code has no detached hook runner, so the entry runs inline within its timeout and its verdict is advisory: never a block.
- After `HookConfig::parse()`, the parser stamps each CC row with `dialect: 'claude'` and `advisory: bool`. Native `hooks.yaml` cannot spell either key, because `HookConfig::ENTRY_KEYS` refuses them.
- `ScriptHook::fromConfig()` reads both flags. Under the claude dialect, 0 allows or reads the envelope and 2 blocks. Any other code becomes allow plus a human notice through `RuntimeNoticeSink::record()`, which crosses forks. Advisory rows downgrade every non-allow the same way.
- The notice helper is a small private method that C-EXT-6.a reuses.
- Unknown types and other keys still refuse in this step; C-EXT-1.b turns them into skip-and-record. That keeps every commit from skipping anything silently.
C-EXT-1.a.files.modify: `candy-code/src/Hooks/ClaudeSettingsHooks.php` (ENTRY_KEYS, `parse()` row build, post-parse dialect stamp), `candy-code/src/Hooks/ScriptHook.php` (constructor flags, `fromConfig()`, the exit `match` at :782), `candy-code/lang/en.php` (`hooks.notice.*`), `candy-code/docs/HOOKS.md` ("What is read from a Claude settings file", "The exit-code contract")

Modify `candy-code/tests/Hooks/ClaudeSettingsHooksTest.php` (`statusMessage` becomes the description; `async` sets advisory; the native validator is still the one used).
C-EXT-1.a.docs/guards: `docs/HOOKS.md`. Check whether `DocFigureProseDriftTest`'s HOOKS.md entry-key pin covers the CC bullets, and move it if so. No child-lifetime change.

C-EXT-1.b.title: Skip-and-record unsupported CC entries, file-qualified names, `~/.claude/settings.json` in policy freshness
C-EXT-1.b.item: C-EXT-1 (sources: INT-4-P1, INT-4-P2, INT-4-P3, GAP-HK-07, p1-miss: CC hook `type: prompt|agent`)
C-EXT-1.b.approach:
- **Root causes.**
- `ClaudeSettingsHooks.php:257-265` refuses the launch for any non-`command` type.
- `:269` names rows `cc:{event}:{index}` with a per-file index, so a user `PreToolUse` plus a trusted project `PreToolUse` collide. `HookManager.php:156-160` throws on that, and `tests/Cli/BootstrapHookFileTest.php:866-878` pins the refusal.
- `Bootstrap::checkPolicyFreshness()` (`Bootstrap.php:4391-4460`) fingerprints only `config.json` and `hooks.yaml` (INT-4-P2).
- `docs/HOOKS.md:59-74` still claims refusals the code no longer makes (INT-4-P3).
- **Fix.**
- `prompt`, `agent`, `http` and `mcp_tool` types, plus unknown entry keys (`if`, `once`, …), are skipped and recorded in a `skippedEntries()` accumulator holding type or key, event and file.
- `reportSkippedClaudeSettingsEvents()` widens its single aggregate row to name skipped events, types and keys. The launch-cap census entry stays at 1; the format constant changes.
- `fromFile($path, string $scope)` names rows `cc:{user|project|local}:{event}:{index}`. `local` comes from `settings.local.json`. `hookFileEntries()` passes `user` for `userClaudeSettingsFile()`.
- The policy snapshot gains a `userClaudeSettings` fingerprint that feeds `$userChanged`. `PolicySnapshot::VERSION` goes 1→2; a version mismatch reads as null, so the one-time name churn quarantines nothing.

C-EXT-7.a.item: C-EXT-7 (sources: VIS-3-P2, PLG-1-P4; VIS-4-P1 is closed in C-EXT-5.b)
C-EXT-7.a.approach:

C-EXT-2.a.title: Skill resources: `asset` loads, resource listing, `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`
C-EXT-2.a.approach:
- **What's dormant.** `SkillLoader::loadSkillAsset()` (`SkillLoader.php:1054`, containment-checked through `ContainedPath::within`) has no caller. Read is jailed to the project root, so a user-tier skill's `scripts/` and `references/` are unreachable except by Bash.

- The Skill tool gains an optional `asset` argument: a relative path under `scripts/`, `references/` or `assets/`. The tool returns that file through `loadSkillAsset()` instead of the body, under the same two header lines.
- Body results list up to 10 sampled resource paths, the OpenCode behaviour.
- `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` and `${SKILL_DIR}` in a body become the base dir.

C-EXT-2.b.title: Honour skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools`/`model`/`effort` for the active turn
C-EXT-2.b.item: C-EXT-2 (sources: GAP-SKL-11, k2-dorm inert frontmatter, k1-dorm#8)
C-EXT-2.b.approach:
- **What's inert.** `FrontmatterKeyAudit.php:120-135` lists four skill keys as INERT; nothing on a live path reads them. Two traps:
- `Skill::$effort` defaults to `'medium'` when absent (`Skill.php:24`), so "declared" cannot be told from "default". Add a nullable or `effortSet` sentinel, per the house law.
- The eight built-ins declare `allowed-tools: "Read,Grep,Bash"` and `effort: high`.
- **Design.** Create `ActiveSkillEffects`. It is pure and derived from the turn's own messages since the last real user prompt: skills loaded by successful `Skill` calls (`SkillTool::invokedIn`) and by `$name` mentions (`TurnContextBlock::invokedSkillsIn`, :467), resolved through the registry. It yields:
- allow rules (CC grammar through `PermissionRule::fromClaudePrefixDialect`, :1305);
- deny rules;
- the latest declared model;
- the latest declared effort.
- **Gate.** `PermissionGate::withTurnGrants($allow, $deny)` returns a clone. Deny rules refuse before the mode, like a configured deny. Allow rules only answer an Ask, with the session-rule semantics of `withSessionRules()` at :389.
- **Wiring.**
- `Runtime::gate()` (:3136) evaluates through a gate carrying the turn's effects, using the PermissionGateHook swap idiom that mode switches use.
- The `Runtime::run()` step loop applies the effects' model and effort to the next request.
- `Chat::gateToolCall()` (:4664) applies the grants on the TUI-side path.
- The four SKILL rows leave INERT.
- **Stateless on purpose.** Skill and gate calls can run in forked children, so in-memory turn state would be lost.

C-EXT-2.c.title: Forked skills (`context: fork`) via the turn-bound Task tool
C-EXT-2.c.approach:
- **What's dormant.** `App::dispatchSkill()` (`App.php:2528`) has no production caller; it is a single-shot pool run. `SkillTool::execute()` loads every skill inline.
- **SkillTool fork path.**
- SkillTool gains `withForkDelegate(TaskTool)`. `EngineBackend::turnTools()` (:3148) binds every SkillTool to the turn's BOUND Task copy after its loop, so the engine, permission relay, emitter and spend all ride the Task path.
- For an `isContextFork()` skill, SkillTool calls a new non-schema `TaskTool::runForkedSkill()`. That method reuses `runOnEngine` with the skill's `agent` (default roster preset `coder`), its model and effort, and the body plus args as the prompt.
- SkillTool becomes `ExemptFromParallelDeadline`.
- With no delegate bound, the skill loads inline with a one-line note.
- **Mentions.** A `$name` or `/name` mention of a fork skill attaches a directive to invoke it through the Skill tool, not the inline body.
- **Skill frontmatter.** `agent` joins KNOWN for skills; `context` leaves INERT.
- **`App::dispatchSkill()` consolidation.** Its Agent construction (env block at root, skill model) moves into a shared `SkillFork`, and `dispatchSkill()` delegates to it. It stays an embedder API; nothing is deleted.
- **Status text.** The App picker's `tui.app.skill_fork` status is reworded to say the skill runs forked when invoked.

C-EXT-3.a.title: `/skills reload` delivered as a turn-context roster delta

- **Problem.** The roster is read once per launch, and the listing sits in the frozen system prompt.

C-EXT-3.d.title: `/agents new` drafts, `/agents accept` promotes
C-EXT-3.d.approach:
- **Why the GAP's plan fails.** The GAP proposes a canned prompt that Writes `.candy-code/agents/<name>.md`. `ProtectFilesHook::WRITE_ONLY_PATTERNS` (`ProtectFilesHook.php:244`) denies that path outright, because a preset's `permissionMode:` is a self-grant. The agent therefore cannot write it.
- **Design.**
- Create a `NewAgentPrompt`, mirroring `NewRulePrompt`. It asks the agent to draft `.candy-code/agents-proposed/<name>.md` (an ordinary, gated write), validated against `FrontmatterKeyAudit::KNOWN[AGENT]`, never overwriting, and listing the existing presets.
- `/agents accept <name>` is a host-side, user-initiated step. It validates the frontmatter, prints the policy keys (`permissionMode`, `tools`, `mcpServers`) and moves the file into `.candy-code/agents/`.
- `/agents proposed` lists the drafts.
- **Routing.** In the TUI, `Chat::handleAgentsCommand()` (:12930) sends `new` to `withInputBuf(prompt)->submit()`, the `/newrule` idiom. On serve, `AgentsHostCommand` returns a SubmitPrompt effect for `new` and handles `accept`/`proposed` itself.
C-EXT-3.d.tests: create `candy-code/tests/Host/Commands/AgentsNewAcceptTest.php` (the prompt shape; accept validates, shows policy keys and moves; refuses an existing name). Modify `candy-code/tests/Chat/PaletteSupersetDispatchTest.php` only if the `/agents` bare form changes (it should not).
C-EXT-3.d.risks: collides with C-AGT-4 (`/agent use`, Tab cycle) on AgentsHostCommand and `handleAgentsCommand`. Put the two in different waves.

C-EXT-3.e.title: Self-learning skills: SkillWorkshop tool + versioned drafts + history/undo
C-EXT-3.e.approach:
- **Tool.** A `SkillWorkshop` tool (Write class, so it is asked in default mode) lets the model create or patch a skill during a turn.
- **Store.** Writes land in a versioned store, `LearnedSkills`. It wraps `ProposedSkills`; each revision is a `LearnedSkillRevision` kept under `history/<n>.md`, with bounded revisions and archive. Names, descriptions and bodies use `ProposedSkills`' caps and sanitizer.
- **Commands.** `/skills history <name>` and `/skills undo <name>` are new.
- **Background review.** The dream pass already drafts skills (`memory.dreamProposeSkills`) and stays the review leg, so no new trigger is added.
- **Default.** Workshop output stays a draft behind `/skills accept`. R-EXT-2 decides whether it may go live with announce-and-undo, as OpenClaw does.

C-EXT-5.a.title: PaletteCatalog core (action + prefill rows)
C-EXT-5.a.approach: a pure `PaletteCatalog::rows(list<CommandSpec> $slashRows): list<PaletteEntry>`. It emits every `PaletteAction` row, with order and labels unchanged. It then adds one Prefill row per slash-visible spec that has no `paletteAction`: built-in survivors, file commands with their tier badge, and MCP prompts badged `[mcp]`. A Prefill label is `/<name> <argument-hint>`. The slash prefix means it can never collide with an action label. Rows are deduped. `PaletteEntryKind` is an enum, in its own file.

C-EXT-5.b.title: Palette shows every slash command, file command and MCP prompt
C-EXT-5.b.approach:
- **Root cause.** `Chat::paletteItemLabels()`'s default arm (:16790) lists only `PaletteAction::all()`, and `runPaletteAction()` (:10491) throws on any other label. The 15 `SLASH_ONLY_SURVIVORS` (`PaletteSupersetDispatchTest.php:57-90`), file commands and MCP prompts therefore never appear.

- The default arm uses `PaletteCatalog::rows($this->slashCommandRows())`.
- A Prefill entry in `runPaletteAction`/`runRootPaletteAction` (:17152) closes the palette and writes `/<name> ` into a BLANK draft, caret at the end.
- A non-blank draft is kept, with a one-line notice: the draft-preservation law.
- Prefill is allowed mid-turn, because it only edits the draft. MRU records it.
- **VIS-4-P1.** The `PaletteAction.php:47-54` docblock is reworded to the full-superset truth. The COMMANDS.md palette paragraph changes too.

C-EXT-5.c.approach:
- **Setting.** `keybindings` accepts `"command:<name>": "<chord>"`. `KeyBindingsValidator::validate()` (:42) checks the name syntactically (colon allowed, for bundle and MCP names) and the chord with the existing parser. `collisionNotices()` reports a collision with a shipped chord.

C-EXT-4.a.title: Marketplace core: manifest reader, registry, provenance, search, recommender
C-EXT-4.a.item: C-EXT-4 (sources: GAP-PLG-02, GAP-SKL-09, p1-miss plugin registry tier, CC-new#12 recommendations)
C-EXT-4.a.approach:
- **`Marketplace`.** Parses Claude's `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: name, owner, `plugins[]` with a source (relative path, `{source:github,repo}` or `{source:url|git,url}`), description, version, keywords/tags/category. It validates names with the bundle-name rule and resolves relative sources inside the checkout through `ContainedPath` (absolute or escaping sources are refused).
- **`MarketplaceRegistry`.** A user-tier record, `~/.candy-code/marketplaces.json` (name → source, pinned sha, addedAt), with checkouts under `~/.candy-code/marketplaces/<name>/`. It follows the `HomeDirectory::owned()` law and writes atomically.
- **`BundleSource`.** The install provenance record, `<bundle>/.candy-code-source.json`.
- **`BundleRecommender`.** Offline: it matches root manifest signals (composer.json, package.json, Dockerfile, `*.tf`, go.mod) against entry keywords and reports at most 3 bundles that are not installed.
- **Search and pin.** Search is lexical. The SHA pin is read from `.git/HEAD`/packed-refs before `.git` is stripped, so no new spawn site is needed.
C-EXT-4.a.docs/guards: ReadPathCensusTest and ContainedPathInventoryTest rows for the new user-tier reads; one type per file.
C-EXT-4.a.risks: Claude's manifest format drifts upstream, so tolerate unknown keys.

C-EXT-4.b.title: `bundles marketplace add/list/remove/update`, `install name@mkt`, `update`, `search`, `recommend`
C-EXT-4.b.approach:
`Subcommands::bundles()` (:1464) gains these verbs:
- **`marketplace add <git-url|path>`.** Clones with the EXISTING `bundlesCloneDefault()` spawn into a scratch dir, validates, pins the SHA, strips `.git` and renames into place.
- **`marketplace list`** and **`marketplace remove`**.
- **`marketplace update [<name>]`.** Re-clones, prints added and removed entries, and moves the pin.
- **`install <plugin>@<marketplace>`.** A relative source copies through C-SEC-1's hardened `copyBundleTree`; a git source uses the existing clone arm. It writes a `BundleSource` record.
- **`update [<bundle>]`.** Re-installs from the recorded `BundleSource` into a scratch dir, then swaps: the old copy moves aside and is removed with no-follow.
- **`search <q>`** and **`recommend`**, with text or `--output-format json`.
- The step also updates the completion roster (`Subcommands.php:2586`) and `cli.bundles.usage`.
- There is no new spawn site, so the child-lifetime roster does not change. Verify that.

C-MCP-1.b.title: Deferred `mcp_call` keeps `mcp__*` hooks and exact Allow grants
C-MCP-1.b.approach:
Root cause (hooks): `HookRegistry::findMatches()` tests each matcher against the bare `$toolName` (`candy-code/src/Hooks/HookRegistry.php:191-211`), fed `$context->toolName` by `executeHooks()` (`:875`) and `chainBudgetSeconds()` (`:637-641`). A deferred call arrives as `mcp_call`, so `mcp__srv__.*` hooks stop firing. That includes the built-in `ProtectFilesHook`, whose matcher is `^(…|mcp__.*)$` (`src/Hooks/BuiltIn/ProtectFilesHook.php:430`) — design-pass finding: deferred MCP calls also escape the secret-file guard.
Fix (hooks): when the subject is `mcp_call` and `McpToolBridge::dispatchedWireName($args)` resolves, a matcher matches on either spelling. `findMatches()` gains an optional `array $toolArgs = []`, and both internal callers pass `$context->toolArgs`. `ProtectFilesHook`'s `default => leafSpellings($args)` already walks nested `arguments`. The script payload keeps `tool_name: mcp_call` with server and tool inside `tool_input`, and the docs say so.
Root cause (grants): `PermissionRule::namesCall()` returns false for every Allow before the MCP parity leg (`candy-code/src/Permissions/PermissionRule.php:516-518`). Fix (grants): an EXACT (glob-free, argument-free) `Allow mcp__s__t` also matches `mcp_call{server:s,tool:t}`. Glob Allows and `Allow mcp_call` stay untranslated ("a grant covers what it names").

C-MCP-6.a.title: MCP hygiene: `mcp_list` lookup, login-URL scan, SSE fork TLS
C-MCP-6.a.kind: fix · MINOR (the login-URL leg is upgraded, see the first bullet) · effort S
C-MCP-6.a.approach:
Three legs, one lane, disjoint files.
- **Login URL (upgrade).** `McpLoginFork::poll()` keeps a 1500-byte tail (`candy-code/src/Support/McpLoginFork.php:35,116`) and takes the FIRST `https?://\S+` (`:120`). The real child prints ``Open this URL in a browser to authorize `<serverUrl>`:`` BEFORE the authorize URL (`candy-code/src/MCP/OAuthLoopbackFlow.php:158-160`). So the TUI announces the server URL (with a trailing `` `: ``), not the login link, on every real flow. The existing test stubs print only the URL (`tests/Chat/McpLoginForkTest.php:90`). Fix: accumulate an un-truncated scan buffer (capped at 64 KiB) until announced, and take the first line consisting solely of one URL (`^\s+(https?://\S+)\s*$`m, the shape `OAuthLoopbackFlow` prints at :160). Expose the parsed `redirect_uri` port for C-MCP-4.c.
- **`mcp_list`.** It truncates at 64 KiB with only a `server` filter (`candy-code/src/Tools/BuiltIn/McpListTool.php:79-92,131`). Add a `tool` argument (exact name → that schema only). When an unfiltered or server-filtered listing would exceed the cap, return a names-plus-one-line overview that says how to fetch each schema.
- **SSE fork.** `SseMcpServer::openStream()` overwrites `$this->socket` (`candy-code/src/MCP/SseMcpServer.php:413`). In a forked child this frees the inherited TLS resource, whose `SSL_shutdown` puts `close_notify` on the parent's connection. Fix: when the current pid is not the opener, retain the inherited resource (never close it) before replacing it.
- **VIS-3-P1.** The stale COMPARISON.md:788 sentence is already absent from the rewritten `candy-code/COMPARISON.md` (grep `launch-time entry bytes` = 0 at design time). Re-grep only; COMPARISON.md is orchestrator-owned, so do not edit it.

Modify `candy-code/tests/MCP/McpDispatcherToolsTest.php`: a roster above the cap stays reachable through `tool`, and the overview names every tool. Create `candy-code/tests/MCP/SseMcpServerForkTlsTest.php`: a forked child's `openStream` leaves the parent's inherited resource open (plain-tcp stub; the TLS alert itself is PLAUSIBLE, not observable in-suite).

- The buffered POST path stays the default.

C-MCP-3.d.title: Long MCP calls continue in background
C-MCP-3.d.approach:
Claude Code moves MCP calls running past 2 minutes to background tasks; candy-code has no equivalent (MCP-N2).
- A bridged or dispatched call runs in a forked grandchild (the house `Support/ForkedChild` helper). The library's fork safety already lets any forked process exchange on a shared server.
- The turn waits with the existing `onWait` beats.
- At 120 s (fixed, CC parity) the tool returns "still running as background MCP job `<id>`; the result will arrive as a message". The grandchild keeps the exchange and writes its result payload under a registry directory (`McpBackgroundCalls`).
- A `McpBackgroundInbox` (`TurnInbox`) composed at `EngineBackend.php:5022` delivers finished results at the next step boundary, or the next turn.
- Fast calls are byte-identical to today.
- `-p` never backgrounds: it waits for the result, as now.
C-MCP-3.d.docs/guards: the fork census (`candy-code/tests/Support/ForkedChildExitConventionTest.php`) for the new fork site. Any `proc_open` must go through `ProcessContainment::spawnSpec` and get a `candy-code/tests/Support/DescriptorInheritanceGuardTest.php` roster row. `LangParityTest`.
C-MCP-3.d.ruling: Background stdio calls hold that server's exchange lock until they finish, so later calls to the same server queue behind them. Accept, or background http/sse servers only?
C-MCP-3.d.risks: a backgrounded call that never answers is bounded only by `toolTimeout`, which keeps its meaning; the turn no longer blocks on it.

- Forked turns and sub-agents inherit the parent's memoised client, so the next turn sees the change.
- The served path works through `McpAuthHostCommand` → `command.exec` with no protocol change.

C-MCP-4.c.title: Served `/mcp login` + paste-back finish from a remote browser
C-MCP-4.c.approach:
In the TUI, `Chat::handleMcpAuthCommand` intercepts `login <server>` into `McpLoginFork` (`candy-code/src/Chat.php:19810-19843`). Served `/mcp login` reaches `McpAuthHostCommand` → `printLoginGuidance()`, which only prints shell guidance (`candy-code/src/Host/Commands/McpAuthHostCommand.php:20-27`). And a remote browser can never reach the child's `127.0.0.1` callback.
- (1) `McpAuthHostCommand` intercepts `login <server>` like Chat, arms `McpLoginFork`, and registers the slot with a new `ServedMcpLogins` watcher (server → sessionId). `ServerContext::pump()` polls it and appends uiOnly rows (link, done/failed) through a new `SessionHost::appendNotice()`, which emits `message.created`.
- (2) Paste-back: `login <server> --code <redirected-url>` is handled inside `McpLoginFork::arm()` when a slot is live. It accepts only `http://127.0.0.1|localhost:<the slot's redirect port>/…`, then issues a local GET to that loopback URL, so the waiting child finishes its own state and PKCE exchange. That works in the TUI too with no Chat change (Chat already forwards `rest`).
- Anything else is refused (no SSRF). Tokens still attach at the next launch (existing honesty).

C-MCP-5.a.title: `mcp serve` core: stdio JSON-RPC host over read-only tools
C-MCP-5.a.approach:
candy-code cannot act as an MCP server: no server-mode code exists, and `docs/MCP.md:880-890` says `serve` "speaks no MCP".
- `McpServeHost` runs an NDJSON JSON-RPC loop on stdin/stdout, framed with `SugarCraft\McpClient\McpMessage`. It answers `initialize` (advertising `tools` only), `notifications/initialized`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`; everything else gets -32601; EOF exits 0.
- `McpServeRoster` builds exactly Read, Glob, Grep, Ls and RepoMap through `ToolCatalog::build(ToolBuildContext)` for `--root`, exposing their schemas.
- Every call goes through the launch's `PermissionGate` and the PreToolUse chain (`ProtectFilesHook` included), built the way `-p` builds its gate.
- An `Ask` verdict is refused (nobody to ask); exec-class and write-class tools are never listed or callable.
- Results are text content; tool errors come back as `isError: true`.
- No session, prompt or memory exposure.
C-MCP-5.a.docs/guards: `php tools/check-one-type-per-file.php`; no new `proc_open` (Grep's `rg` spawn is an existing site).
C-MCP-5.a.ruling: Confirm scope: stdio only, a read-only roster (Read/Glob/Grep/Ls/RepoMap), Ask → refuse, and no session or prompt exposure?
C-MCP-5.a.risks: the gate's path containment must hold for an external caller with no TUI, so pin a `../` read refusal.

P-MENU.b.title: `ShellMenu`: the five-menu tree
P-MENU.b.approach:
- **Builder.** `ShellMenu::tree(?App $a = null, ?list<CommandSpec> $rows = null): MenuTree` builds the tree in "Proposed menu tree" from a nested `PLACEMENT` const keyed by command **name**. Dispatch can then go by name, and a repeated label can never run the wrong row.
- **Keeps MenuBar's "derived, not declared" law** (`MenuBar.php:59-73`):
- every leaf is a live `CommandRegistry::all()` spec labelled `$spec->label()`;
- a PLACEMENT name the registry lacks fails the test; it never becomes a ghost row;
- a registry row PLACEMENT does not name still lands at runtime in `App ▸ More ▸` (`tui.menu.sub.more`), so it is never unreachable, AND it fails `ShellMenuTest`, so its author has to place it.
- `HIDDEN = ['generate']`.
- **Panes ▸** comes from `Pane::tabCycle()`, with one `toggle()` per pane:
- `checked` is `$a->isDocked($pane)`; Chat is always checked and focus-only;
- icon `Pane::icon()`, label `Pane::label()`, id `pane:<value>`.
With `$a === null` every check is false but the structure is identical, so keyboard navigation needs no App.
- **Menu-only label.** The `generate-form` row reads `Generate image…` (`tui.menu.item.generate_image`). The palette label and `MediaFormKeysTest:211` (`runPaletteAction('Generate image')`) stay untouched.
- Nothing reads `ShellMenu` until P-MENU.d. The step ships the tree and its guard.

P-MENU.c.title: Menu overlay seam: every frame paints, clamps and scans the open menu
P-MENU.c.item: P-MENU-REDO (sources: owner pick; latent bugs 1–3 above)
P-MENU.c.approach:
- **Root causes.** All three are read from source; the lane's regression tests must go red first.
1. `renderAgentDashboard()` overlays nothing and scans titles only (`src/Tui/Renderer.php:905-927`). Yet F10 (`KeyboardHandler.php:151-153`) and a title click (`App.php:3387-3392`) still open a menu there, so the menu is invisible while it owns the keyboard.
2. `renderVideoPlayer()` scans row zones (`:1036`) it never paints.
3. `overlayDropdown()` (`:2145`) splices at `MenuBar::activeMenuColumn()`, which counts unpainted titles (`MenuBar.php:588-605`), and `spliceInto()` (`:2299`) never clamps to `$cols`. The result is an over-wide frame line at 80 cols.
- **Fix.**
- One `overlayMenu(App, string $frame, int $cols, int $top): string` splices every `MenuPanel` from `MenuBar::panels()`, clamped to `$cols`.
- One panel pass in `scanChrome()` reads `MenuBar::panelsMarked()`.
- All five frame paths call both: `renderView`, `renderAgentDashboard`, `renderMediaForm`, `renderVideoPlayer` and `renderSettingsEditor`.
- **Behaviour is preserved.**
- In this step `MenuBar::panels()`/`panelsMarked()` return today's single dropdown as one `MenuPanel`, shifted left to fit. P-MENU.d swaps in the cascade without touching `Tui/Renderer.php` again.
- `renderDropdown()`/`renderDropdownMarked()` stay as forwarders, since tests read them.
- `overlayMenu()` runs after P-IMG.b's veil composite, so the menu draws crisply above the popup.

P-MENU.d.item: P-MENU-REDO (sources: owner pick; supersedes P-IMG.a; latent bug 4)
P-MENU.d.approach:
- **MenuBar.**
- `menus()` reads the `ShellMenu::tree()` titles.
- The static `$activeMenu`/`$activeItem` pair becomes one static `MenuCursor`.
- `handleKey()` is `MenuCursor::key()`, and `selectItem()` takes a path (an int still means a root row).
- `panels()` returns the `MenuCascade`, and `activeMenuColumn()` counts painted titles only.
- The deprecated `get*` forwarders stay.
- **Narrow widths.** Titles drop from the right into a `»` title (`tui.menu.more`). Its dropdown lists the dropped menus as submenus, so every row stays reachable at any width; this is P-IMG.a's overflow idea, done through the nested model. The tab strip stays in this step (P-MENU.e moves it), so the titles keep today's budget rule.
- **Dispatch by name.**
- Leaves raise `MenuSelectedMsg(menu, label, action: 'cmd:<name>' | 'pane:<value>')`.
- `App::dispatchMenuSelection()` sends `cmd:` to `runRegistryCommand($name)`, with the same settings-view rule (:4000). It sends `pane:` to a `togglePaneFromChrome(Pane)` extracted from the `panetab:` click arm (:3468-3482), so a keyboard toggle and a click are one door.
- With `action === null`, the label lookup stays. `AppModelTest`, `MenuCommandDraftPreservationTest` and `SettingsCommandTest` build label-only messages and do not move.
- **Bug 4 (root cause).** While a menu is open, a key the menu answers returns from the open-menu block (`KeyboardHandler.php:591-603`). It never reaches the skill picker (:612) or `handleNavigation()` (:632).
- **KeyBindingRegistry `menu()`** (:1327-1337):
- `menu.switch` (`← / →`, from a leaf row) is kept;
- new `menu.submenu` (`→ / ←`: open the highlighted submenu, then close it again);
- `menu.run` is reworded to "Run the row, or open its submenu (or o)";
- `menu.close` is reworded to "Close the submenu, then the menu (or q)".
Each two-effect row is driven both ways, per the drift test's own rule (`KeyBindingDriftTest.php:78-88`).
- **Pane tabs.** They stay on the bar for this one step. View ▸ Panes rows carry `menuitem:` zones here and toggle by keyboard and click; P-MENU.e moves the `panetab:` zones onto them.
P-MENU.d.docs/guards:

- `KeyBindingDriftTest` moves in-step with the `menu.*` rows.

P-MENU.e.title: Pane toggles leave the bar: View ▸ Panes owns `panetab:`, hover, indicator door
P-MENU.e.approach:
- **The bar.**
- `compose()` drops the pane-tab strip and its three densities (`MenuBar.php:94-114`, :220-288).
- The right end keeps only the `Currently: <pane>` indicator (R-MENU-2). It goes terse (label only) below 61 cols and disappears below 50, so the five titles always come first.
- The indicator becomes a click door, zone `panesmenu`, that opens View ▸ Panes.
- **One list.** `PANE_TABS` (:94-102) is folded into `Pane::tabCycle()`, the list `PaneReverseCycleTest` already pins it equal to. Later panes (P-CTX.e's Context, P-TABS.g's Sessions) therefore appear in View ▸ Panes with no MenuBar edit. This is consolidation; no code is deleted.
- **The `panetab:<pane>` zone moves from the bar to the Panes rows.** `ShellMenu` sets each toggle node's `zone`. The existing click arm (`App.php:3468`) and the drag-to-dock arm (`dragTargetPane()`, :3071) stay wired unchanged:
- a click toggles docking;
- a press-drag on a docked pane's row carries the pane to a side, and `beginPaneDrag()` closes the menu once the drag arms;
- toggling keeps the submenu open and flips the check in place (R-MENU-3).
The rows keep the old tab's three states: focused is `shellPrimary` bold underlined, docked is ✓ in `shellForeground`, undocked is blank in `shellMuted`.
- **Hover.**
- **Mouse mode.** CellMotion reports no button-less motion (`Chat.php:6034`). So while any menu is open, the shell arms `Cmd::enableMouseAllMotion()`, and it restores `Cmd::enableMouseCellMotion()` when the menu closes. This is ONE transition check in `App::update()` (:2714), comparing `MenuBar::activeMenu() > 0` before and after every message, so every close path is covered. It is skipped when the mouse is Off.
- **Motion routing.** While a menu is open, `handleShellMouse()` (:2883) consumes motion. Over a `menuitem:` or `panetab:` row it calls `MenuBar::hover()` (highlight; a submenu row expands). Anywhere else the motion is swallowed, so the chat never receives hover.
P-MENU.e.docs/guards: README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md prose. No generated roster moves. The `mouse.*` key rows do not change, so `KeyBindingDriftTest` does not move.
P-MENU.e.ruling: R-MENU-2 (keep the `Currently:` indicator as a door to View ▸ Panes; default yes) and R-MENU-3 (the submenu stays open after a toggle; default yes)
P-MENU.e.risks: AllMotion floods the read loop, but only while a menu is open. A missed close path would leave it on, so the single transition check and MenuHoverTest's close-path table are the guard.

P-TABS.e.title: App hosts many Chats: scoped routing, park/unpark, background streaming (GAP-SES-12)
P-TABS.e.approach:
- `App` gains a `SessionDeck`. Every Cmd a Chat returns, from `delegateToChat` (:4298), `runRegistryCommand` and `feedChat`, is wrapped by `TabScope::cmd($fgKey)`. App-level Cmds stay unscoped, so shell Msgs (SettingsSaved…) can never be misrouted.
- A new `TabScopedMsg` arm in `update()` (:2714) does the routing:
- **foreground:** unwrap and re-enter `update()`;
- **parked:** `$parked->update($inner)`, re-wrap its Cmd, and refresh that tab's attention (inFlight → Working; pendingPermission → Waiting; reply settled while parked → Unseen; error → Failed).
- Shell-claimed inner Msgs from a parked tab are dropped (OpenMediaForm/OpenSettings/OpenAgentView), except AgentMessageSentMsg, which is keyed by run. A background tab can never pop a modal; it raises attention instead.
- `subscriptions()` (:4664) merges each parked Chat's `TabScope::subscriptions()`. The foreground-only ids are the background poll, statusLine and idle-compact.
- **Switch:** park the foreground Chat (its turn keeps running), unpark or factory-build the target, replay `WindowSizeMsg($cols,$rows)` (`handleWindowSize`, :4265), and move the notice drain to the new foreground via a new `Chat::withNoticeDrain(bool)` (the field exists, `src/Chat.php:1440`).
- The App intercepts Ctrl+Tab/Ctrl+Shift+Tab and Ctrl+N (shell.new-session) when the deck is armed. After each delegate it rekeys the deck when `currentSessionId()` moved in place (`/branch`, mint).
- **Close:** closing a busy tab needs a second press within 3 s (`cancel and close`); then it cancels, flushes and releases the lock.
- **Quit** with busy background tabs asks once.
- No new fork site: each tab's turn uses the existing TurnRunner/EngineBackend fork path. TurnRunner is already keyed per token and session (`src/Host/TurnRunner.php:643-734`).

P-AGENT.b.item: P-AGENT-ATTACH (sources: owner pick; CLAW-new#7 note; CC-new#9 parity note only)
P-AGENT.b.approach:
- **Gap 1: shared viewport.** The Agent View shares the main chat's scroll and draft. `App::openAgentView`/`closeAgentView` (`src/App/App.php:710,810`) never save `Chat::scrollOffset()` or the input, so the main draft becomes the agent composer and the scroll position leaks across.

- Chat gains public `draft()`/`withDraft(text, cursor)`; `withInputBuf` is private (:15672). `withScrollOffset` exists (:7158).
- The open agent view is remembered per tab, so switching tabs and back restores it.
- **Gap 2: no session-level list of agents.** `App::windowList()` adds each session's live runs (`forSession`) as child entries:
- the SessionsPane agent rows and the strip chip (`▸ ⠋ @explore` in preset colour);
- ⏳ when the run waits on you (`AskOrigin`);
- a click switches tab if needed, then `openAgentView`.
- **Gap 3: delivery is steer-only.** User messages reach a running child only at its next step boundary (`AgentInbox::send` → mailbox → `MailboxTurnInbox` drained at the child's step boundary, `src/Tools/BuiltIn/TaskTool.php:1544`).
- Add `Ctrl+X i`: send the draft as `MessageMode::Interrupt`, which skips the step's unstarted calls and reads the message first (`src/Agents/Live/MessageMode.php`).
- Wiring: a new `AgentControlMsg::INTERRUPT` verb → `Chat::submitToAgents` (~:9142) passes the mode. The sent row reads `⚡ interrupt` vs `⧗ queued`.

C-CTX-2.a.title: Drain the runtime-notice sink in serve
C-CTX-2.a.item: C-CTX-2 (sources: GAP-MEM-10w, k1-sum (a), k1-dorm#1, MOD-14 web)
C-CTX-2.a.approach:
- Root cause: serve arms the process sink in `Bootstrap::workspace()` (`candy-code/src/Cli/Bootstrap.php:1678-1679`), but the only `drain()` is `Chat::pumpRuntimeNotices()` (`candy-code/src/Chat.php:18636`). On served sessions, recall rows, FallbackProvider switch notices and parser warnings vanish.
- The per-session seam already exists and has no production caller: `NoticeSink` instances plus `RuntimeNoticeSink::using()` (`RuntimeNoticeSink.php:715`), which a fork pins through `enterForkedChild()` (`EngineBackend.php:3835`).
- Each `SessionHost` owns its own `NoticeSink`. It is armed cross-fork only when the workspace sink is armed, so tests and embedders stay unarmed.
- Every fork the host starts runs under `RuntimeNoticeSink::using($this->notices, …)`: `dispatch()` around `runner()->start()` and `$run()`, `requestAheadOfNeed()`, and `scheduleGoalJudge()`.
- `TurnRunner::start()` receives `notices: $this->notices` instead of the shared `workspace->notices` (`SessionHost.php:1785`).
- Draining happens on a `notifyOnceWhenPending()` wake (re-armed every time), in `pump()`, and on settle. Each drained row goes through `appendMessageRow(Message::notice(...))`, so it is uiOnly, saved, and announced as `message.created` with kind `notice`, which the web reducer already renders.
- `release()` resets the sink, closing its two fds.
C-CTX-2.a.risks: a parent-side notice raised outside a host's `using()` window (e.g. MCP startup in the workspace process) still lands on the undrained workspace sink. This is stated in SERVER.md and not fixed here.

C-CTX-1.a.title: Prime the instruction-diff tracker before the turn forks
C-CTX-1.a.approach:
- Root cause: `Runtime::instructionDiff()` (`candy-code/src/Runtime.php:5742-5754`) memoises `InstructionDiffTracker::capture($loader)` on the first `turnContext()`, and that runs only inside the forked child.
- `EngineBackend::beginSessionTurn()` (`candy-code/src/Backend/EngineBackend.php:2843-2860`) primes only `primeSessionPrompt()`.
- So every child captures "frozen = current disk" (`InstructionDiffTracker.php:177-190`), `recheck()` finds nothing, and the memo dies with the child. This was reproduced: on a forked turn 2 the diff is absent.
- Fix: add a public `Runtime::primeInstructionDiff(App)` that fills the same `instruction-diffs:<loader id>` slot of the shared `SessionPromptMemo` in the parent.
- Call it in `beginSessionTurn()` right after `primeSessionPrompt()`, inside the same try/catch. Also call it beside the `summariseAsync()` prime (`EngineBackend.php:4425`), so a summary fork never captures post-edit bytes.
- Update the tracker docblock's capture-window limit (`:67-71`).
- What the user sees: a CLAUDE.md edit made mid-session reaches the model on the next TUI or served turn.
C-CTX-1.a.tests: modify `candy-code/tests/Providers/PromptPrefixByteStabilityTest.php`. Add a fork-path twin of `testAMidSessionInstructionEditRidesTheTailRowAndNotTheFrozenPrefix` that drives `completeAsync()` twice (skipped without pcntl). On turn 2 the diff is present and the frozen prefix bytes are unchanged.
C-CTX-1.a.risks: the prime only helps if the parent and child share one `SessionPromptMemo` instance. The test must therefore go through `completeAsync()`, not a direct Runtime call.

C-CTX-1.b.title: Cursor glob rules fire; disabled imported rules are explained
C-CTX-1.b.approach:
- Root cause: `candy-code/src/Context/Rule.php:233-238` ANDs `alwaysApply` into `enabled`. Cursor's canonical Auto-Attached shape (`globs: src/**/*.ts` + `alwaysApply: false`) therefore parses as disabled, and `RuleLoader::load()` drops it (`RuleLoader.php:377`).
- A comma string such as `globs: a/*.ts, b/*.ts` also becomes one never-matching pattern (`Rule.php:277-283` → `stringListField()` :435-450).
- Fix: `alwaysApply: false` disables a rule only when it has no `paths`/`globs`. Path-scoped rules are already deferred to tool time (`Runtime.php:4583-4597`).
- Split comma-string globs into separate patterns, and record a `disabledBy: alwaysApply` reason on the rule.
- `RulesCommand` prints one aggregate hint: "N imported rules are off (`alwaysApply: false`, no globs); turn one on with `/rules <name>`". `RulesHostCommand` reuses that output.
- Document Cursor's mapping table in `docs/MEMORY.md` (:745-750).
C-CTX-1.b.risks: a project that used `alwaysApply:false` to keep a globbed rule OFF now gets it at tool time. The `/rules` toggle is the escape, and the hint names it.

C-CTX-1.c.title: Track `@import` children in the instruction diff
C-CTX-1.c.approach:
- The tracker's declared limit (`InstructionDiffTracker.php:59-63`) leaves a child-only edit to an `@import`ed file invisible until the next refresh point.
- Capture records each root document's resolved import children as stat-only entries. The children come from the loader's existing expansion, through `ImportResolver`.
- `recheck()` stat-gates the children like roots. A changed child renders as the existing degradation line with a `Read <path>` pointer. There is no re-expansion per turn, so the cost model holds.
- Children tracked per document are capped at 32. The docblock limit is removed.

C-CTX-1.c.tests: modify `candy-code/tests/Context/InstructionDiffTurnContextTest.php`. A child-only edit renders one pointer line; an unchanged child costs one stat and renders nothing.

C-PRV-1.a.title: `EffortGate`, a per-model shaper predicate, and Bedrock / Codex / claude-code effort

C-PRV-1.a.approach:
- Root cause: `/effort` gates per provider, through the empty marker `ShapesReasoningEffort` (`candy-code/src/Providers/ShapesReasoningEffort.php:34`).

- Fix part 2: add `Providers\ThinkingCapability`, one per-family table of thinking support and output ceilings, for Anthropic and Gemini families. C-PRV-5.a reuses it.
- Fix part 3: add `Providers\EffortGate` with `verdict(ProviderInterface, model)`, which unwraps a FallbackProvider to its primary, and `shape()`, the status phrase now inlined in `Chat.php:12262-12271`.

C-PRV-1.c.title: Safe `candy-code login`: merge, refuse a type clash, no echo
C-PRV-1.c.approach:
- Root cause 1: `Subcommands::loginStoreKey()` replaces the provider block outright with `$providers[$type] = ['type' => $type, 'apiKey' => $key]` (`candy-code/src/Cli/Subcommands.php:973`). Rotating a key wipes `model`, `thinkingBudget`, `modelPrices` and, worst of all, a gateway `baseUrl`.
- Root cause 2: the key is read with `fgets(\STDIN)` with TTY echo on (`:942`).
- Fix: merge `apiKey` (and `type`) into the existing block, and refuse without writing when the existing block's `type` differs.
- When STDIN is a TTY, read the key with echo off through sugar-core's `SugarCraft\Core\Util\Tty`: raw mode, minimal Enter/Backspace/Ctrl-C handling, restored in `finally`.
- No new child process. The existing `$loginKeyRead` seam keeps the suite TTY-free; add a `$loginTty` seam for the echo-off branch.
C-PRV-1.c.tests: modify `candy-code/tests/Cli/LoginSubcommandTest.php`. `model`, `baseUrl` and `thinkingBudget` survive a key rotation; a mismatched type refuses and leaves the file byte-identical; the tty seam is restored after a thrown read.
C-PRV-1.c.risks: the raw-mode reader must restore the terminal on every exit path, including a SIGINT during the read.

C-PRV-5.a.title: Per-family thinking ceilings and omission
C-PRV-5.a.approach:
- Root cause: the only bound is a floor (`ProviderFactory.php:999-1006`), while the wire sets `max_tokens = max(…, 1.5×budget)` (`AnthropicMessagesWire.php:509-515`).
- These therefore 400 on every turn:
- `thinkingBudget: 50000` (gives `max_tokens: 75000`);
- `/effort low` on `claude-3-5-haiku`;
- `/effort max` on `gemini-2.5-flash` (ceiling 24576);
- any `/effort` on `gemini-2.0-flash`.
- Fix: the Anthropic and Gemini wires read C-PRV-1.a's `ThinkingCapability` table.
- Omit `thinking`/`thinkingConfig` for non-thinking families.
- Clamp the budget to the family ceiling, keeping the 1024 floor.
- Clamp `max_tokens` to the family output ceiling.
- `ProviderFactory` refuses at launch a configured `thinkingBudget` above the largest ceiling of the configured type, with the same loud shape as the floor.
C-PRV-5.a.tests: create ThinkingCeilingTest with per-family wire-body pins: omission on non-thinking families, the clamp on budget and `max_tokens`, and the launch refusal above the ceiling.
C-PRV-5.a.risks: the family table goes stale as models ship. An unknown family keeps today's behaviour (no clamp), so the table never refuses a model it does not know.

C-PRV-5.b.title: No thinking budget on the title and auxiliary backends

C-CTX-6.b.title: PDF page check and an aggregate document budget
C-CTX-6.b.approach:
- Root cause: PDFs have only a per-file 20 MiB cap (`FileMentions.php:58-64`). `AttachmentEncoding.php:87-95` re-encodes every earlier document on every request, so a 15 MB + 10 MB pair puts every later request over 32 MiB and each turn 400s or 413s.
- At attach time, `FileMentions` estimates pages (count `/Type /Page` objects) and refuses above 100 pages with a notice. Compressed object streams that hide the count are allowed through as unknown.
- `EngineBackend::typedUserMessage()` (:5961) keeps a cumulative base64 budget. Older document blocks over it are withheld and replaced by a one-line placeholder ("document <name> withheld; re-attach to resend"), with one notice per turn.
C-CTX-6.b.tests: create DocumentAggregateBudgetTest: with two PDFs the older one is withheld and the newest kept; modify `candy-code/tests/Attachments/FileMentionsTest.php`: a >100-page refusal, and unknown counts pass
C-CTX-6.b.risks: the page heuristic is approximate. It refuses only on a positive count over 100.

C-CTX-5.a.approach:
- Already shipped: `summaryModel`, cache-reusing summaries, a heuristic fold on any summary error, and a stall ceiling.
- Missing 1: a compaction request that itself overflows the window has no second try.
- Missing 2: a configured `summaryModel` that fails non-transiently (unknown model, 4xx) is never retried on the session's model.

- on `ContextOverflow::matches()`, retry once with `CompactionService::clipOlderToolOutputs()` (older tool results cut to head and tail, the newest exchanges kept);
- on a non-transient failure of an overridden summary model, retry once on `engine->withSummaryModel(null)`;
- otherwise reject as today, which folds heuristically.
- Pin CLAW-new#5 parity: a 408, a 504 or an idle-stall rejection lands a heuristic fold, and the parked turn proceeds on both hosts.
C-CTX-5.a.tests: CacheReusingSummaryBackendTest (overflow → one clipped retry; model failure → one session-model retry; transient errors not retried); CompactionFallbackParityTest (TUI and served parked turn both proceed on a heuristic fold after 408/504/stall)

- Each retry is a second billed call. It is capped at one, and the ledger already bills summary calls.

C-SEC-1.a.title: Bundle install never follows symlinks
C-SEC-1.a.approach:
- Root cause: `Subcommands::removeTree()` (`candy-code/src/Cli/Subcommands.php:1920-1935`) recurses on `\is_dir($child)` at :1931, and `is_dir()` follows symlinks. A clone holding `x -> ../../..` therefore empties `$HOME` on every failure exit: :1670 (clone failed), :1683 (no manifest), :1694 (bad name), :1702 (already installed) and :1712-1717 (copy fallback).
- Fix 1: test `is_link()` before `is_dir()` and `unlink()` the link itself, never descending. Apply the same guard to the top-level `$path`.
- Fix 2: add `-c core.symlinks=false` to the clone argv at :1749, so git checks links out as plain files.
- Fix 3 (PLG-1-P3): `copyBundleTree()` (:1877-1913) follows links when it recurses and when it copies (~:1899-1911). It now refuses the install and names the first link it meets, which also ends cyclic-link loops.
C-SEC-1.a.tests:
- modify `candy-code/tests/Bundles/BundleInstallTest.php`:
- Through the `$bundlesInstallSpawn` seam, build a scratch holding `link -> <outside sentinel dir>`, crossed with each of: no manifest, an invalid name, an existing name. Assert the sentinel survives and the scratch is gone.
- A path source holding an outside link is refused, and the message names the link.
- A cyclic link terminates.
- Update the argv pin at :189-197 (`testTheDefaultCloneArgvPinsTheExtTransportOffBeforeTheCloneToken`): its substring `'git', '-c', 'protocol.ext.allow=never', 'clone'` breaks once a second `-c` is inserted. Re-pin both `-c` pairs ahead of `clone`.
C-SEC-1.a.docs/guards: none. The refusal names the link, and no doc page describes the cleanup. Child lifetime: no new spawn.
C-SEC-1.a.deps: none. C-EXT-4 (marketplace) and C-MCP-2 should name this step as a prerequisite.
C-SEC-1.a.risks: a legitimate bundle that ships an in-tree relative symlink now installs as a plain file (clone) or is refused (path). The loaders already refuse links that escape the tree, so nothing that loads today is lost.

C-SEC-2.a.title: Web Edit card shows every edit and the raw arguments
C-SEC-2.a.approach:
- Root cause 1: `diffPairsFor()` (`candy-code-web/src-web/lib/lineDiff.ts:38-41`) returns only the top-level `old_string`/`new_string` pair whenever it is present. `Edit::editList()` (`candy-code/src/Tools/BuiltIn/Edit.php:441-471`) always runs the top-level pair as edit 1 and `edits[]` as edits 2..N, so the `edits`-only branch (:42-52) never matches a real call.

- Fix in `lineDiff.ts`:
- Build the pair list as `[top-level pair, ...edits]`, in the same order as `editList`.
- Return `null` (raw-dump fallback) on any malformed entry, including an empty `old_string` in `edits` (Edit refuses those).
- Read `replace_all` as truthy, top-level and per entry, as `editList` does, and add "(replace all occurrences)" to that pair's label.
- Mark the `<summary>` as snippet-relative (WEB-5-P4) without changing the `@@` grammar that `DiffView` parses.

C-SEC-3.a.title: One provenance-aware `!cmd` gate (refuse MCP and bundle shell forms)
C-SEC-3.a.item: C-SEC-3 (sources: PLG-1-P2, MCP-2-P1, p1 Summary theme, p1-miss "unified third-party shell posture")
C-SEC-3.a.approach:
- Root cause: `TurnController::refuseCommandShell()` (`candy-code/src/Host/TurnController.php:521-575`) gates only the `project` tier (:528) and the `mcp` tier (:545-554), and both legs check only `trustedProjectCommands`. After that, an `Ask` verdict proceeds unprompted (:567-575).
- MCP leg: a remote server's `prompts/get` body runs a shell under a grant meant for the repo's own files. This is pinned as intended at `tests/Host/TurnControllerTest.php:186`.
- Bundle leg: `ForeignCommandDiscovery::bundleDirs()` (:146-152) stamps bundle rows `$bundle->tier`, which is `user` for `~/.candy-code/bundles`, so git-installed bundle commands run `!cmd` unprompted.
- Fix: a `CommandShellPosture` table maps `(tier, source)` to a `ShellProvenance` case:
- operator (user tier): gate only;
- repo (project tier): `trustedProjectCommands`, then the gate;
- third-party (MCP prompt body, or any `SkillSource::Bundle` row whatever its tier): refused, with a Lang notice, before the gate is evaluated.
- `refuseCommandShell()` and `customCommandMustFork()` read the table. A bundle body whose only shell forms are refused no longer forks; an MCP placeholder still forks, for its fetch.
- Foreign rows keep today's behaviour in this step (the tier decides). C-SEC-3.b rules on them.

C-SEC-4.b.title: `context.trust` routable, failed writes surfaced, prompt discoverable
C-SEC-4.b.item: C-SEC-4 (sources: WEB-3-P1, WEB-3-P2, WEB-3-P3, p2-miss "WEB-3 trust prompt discovery")
C-SEC-4.b.approach:
- P1 root cause: the `context.trust` params (`MethodSchemas.php:413-418`) carry no `sessionId`. `Gateway::routeOf()` (`src/Server/Workspace/Gateway.php:289-298`) therefore sends the call to the primary process. The prompt was minted in a workspace-host child (`TrustAsks` is per-process static, :37-41), so every non-primary root gets `ask_not_found` and the prompt loops forever.
- P1 fix: make `sessionId` required. The gateway then routes it like `permission.respond`, with no Gateway change. `TrustAsks::settle()` also verifies that the ask's root equals the session's workspace root.
- P2 root cause: `TrustAsks::settle()` :124-131 drops `$report['error']` and settles `granted, persisted:false`.
- P2 fix: when `remember === 'user'` and the write fails, throw `RpcError` `trust_write_failed` (carrying the report error) and leave the record `asked`.
- P3 root cause: the prompt is minted only by `context.sources`, which runs only when the Context panel mounts.
- P3 fix: `session.subscribe` runs the cheap MCP census (`Bootstrap::mcpServerInventory($root)['status']`) and calls `TrustAsks::discover()`. The web store holds a `pendingTrust` independent of `sources`; it currently drops events while `sources === null` (`contextSources.ts:86-97`). `StatusBar` shows a badge that opens the Context panel.

C-SEC-8.a.title: Fence MCP tool output as untrusted

C-SEC-8.b.title: Opt-in secret redaction of tool output

- Tool results enter history and `sessions.db` raw. `SecretRedactor` (`src/Memory/SecretRedactor.php:79`) covers only memory, audit and `/share`.

- The flag reaches `Runtime` through its existing settings plumbing (a `with*` on construction).

C-SEC-8.c.title: `Sanitize::stripInvisibleFormatting()` in sugar-core
C-SEC-8.c.approach:
- `Sanitize::markInvisibleFormatting()` (`sugar-core/src/Util/Sanitize.php:359`) only marks. It has a two-tier rule: bidi, ZWSP, WJ and BOM are always marked, while ZWJ/ZWNJ/LRM/RLM/ALM are kept after a non-ASCII byte.
- Add a sibling `stripInvisibleFormatting(string $s, ?int &$removed = null)`. It applies the same tiers, deletes instead of marking, and reuses `invisibleFormattingMaps()` so the two can never disagree.

C-SEC-8.d.title: Strip invisible Unicode at submit (TUI and serve)
C-SEC-8.d.approach:
- Invisible formatting is only marked on display today. One rule applies at both submit chokes:
- TUI: `Chat::submit()` (`src/Chat.php:9389`);
- served: `SessionHost::submit()` (`src/Host/SessionHost.php:524`), which `session.send` reaches through `TurnMethods.php:198`.
- Each choke runs `Sanitize::stripInvisibleFormatting()` on the prompt text, not on attachments, and posts one notice with the count when anything was removed.
- No opt-out key: the joiner tier keeps legitimate scripts and emoji. This deliberately departs from the gap's "setting to keep them", to stay off the settings and README rosters, and can be a follow-up if the owner asks.

C-SEC-8.e.title: `${keychain:<name>}` provider keys
C-SEC-8.e.approach:
- Provider keys sit in plaintext in a 0600 config, and `ProviderFactory::resolveEnv()` (`src/Providers/ProviderFactory.php:450`) resolves only `${VAR}`.
- Add `${keychain:<name>}`, resolved by a new `Keychain` that shells out to `secret-tool lookup service candy-code account <name>` on Linux or `security find-generic-password -s candy-code -a <name> -w` on macOS. It uses argv arrays only, through `ProcessContainment::spawnSpec`, and drains then reaps in-function. A short timeout is fine, since this is not an LLM call.
- Resolution is memoised per process. A miss is a launch notice naming the entry, never a fatal.

If `DescriptorInheritanceGuardTest` (`candy-code/tests/Support/DescriptorInheritanceGuardTest.php`) does not classify it `short`, add an `ACCOUNTED_FOR` row there. candy-code's sites are owned by that guard; `tools/check-child-lifetimes.php` excludes candy-code.

C-SES-1.a.title: Headless `-p` spend reaches the ledger; `session list` shows spend
C-SES-1.a.item: C-SES-1 (sources: SES-1-P1, p2-miss: headless `-p` spend, SES-1-P4 `session list` half)
C-SES-1.a.approach:
- **Root cause.** `NonInteractive::run()` collects each step's `Usage` into `$sessionUsages` (`src/Cli/NonInteractive.php:405-409`), but only for the JSON envelope (`:609`). `appendUsageRecord` has exactly two callers, `src/Chat.php:19002` and `src/Host/SessionHost.php:2267`, so a `-p` run persists its session row (the AUT-2 block, `:653-660`) without its money. `/usage`, `/budget` after `--resume`, and `/status`'s ledger row then all under-report.
- **Fix.** In the AUT-2 persist block, after `$mint()`, send each buffered usage through `SpendLedger::new()->account(new TokenTracker(), $usage, $sink, $backend->model())`. The sink calls `EnhancedSessionStore::appendUsageRecord($opened['id'], …)`.
- Gate it on `$ownsSession && $opened !== null && $sessionStore instanceof EnhancedSessionStore`.
- Put it inside the same `try`, so a store failure costs one stderr line and leaves the exit code unchanged (the "store must not cost the answer" law).
- **`session list`.** Its text rows gain the cached spend, printed with `SpendLedger::boundUsd($row->costUnpriced, $row->costUsd)` (`≥` when unpriced, `—` when null). Its `--json` rows gain `spentUsd` and `spendUnpriced`.
- **What the user sees:** `-p` spend in `/usage`, and every row of `candy-code session list` showing its cost.
C-SES-1.a.files.modify: `candy-code/src/Cli/NonInteractive.php` (run(): AUT-2 persist block), `candy-code/src/Cli/Subcommands.php` (sessionList(), sessionLabel()), `candy-code/lang/en.php` (`cli.session.list.spend*`), `candy-code/README.md` (Non-interactive mode: the session-persistence paragraph; Subcommands: the `session list` sample)
C-SES-1.a.docs/guards: the README.md paragraphs only. No new verb, flag or env var, so no roster guard moves.
C-SES-1.a.risks: The lazy mint must run before the first append. Buffering the appends to the persist block guarantees that; never append inside the step observer.

C-SES-1.b.title: Background announcement obeys the `≥` law
C-SES-1.b.approach:
- **Root cause.** `BackgroundSession::announcement()` prints `sprintf('$%.4f', $this->costUsd)` only when the cost is above zero (`src/Background/BackgroundSession.php:327-329`). It ignores `spendUnpriced` (`:77`, `:118-123`): an unpriced background session prints an exact figure, or hides its `≥$0`. The web BackgroundPanel already prints `≥`.
- **Fix.** Print `SpendLedger::boundUsd($this->spendUnpriced, $this->costUsd)` when `costUsd > 0 || spendUnpriced`.
C-SES-1.b.tests: modify `candy-code/tests/Chat/BackgroundResultAnnouncedTest.php`. Pin both polarities, plus unpriced-at-zero printing `≥$0`.
C-SES-1.b.risks: An announcement golden may pin the old `$0.0123` text. Re-pin it in-step.

C-SES-2.a.title: FTS index: one-transaction rebuild + persisted build marker
C-SES-2.a.approach:
- **Root cause.** `SessionSearchIndex::$built` starts `false` in every process (`src/Session/SessionSearchIndex.php:68-70`), so `needsRebuild()` (`:102-105`) is true on each launch's first body search. `EnhancedSessionStore::rebuildSearchIndex()` (`src/Session/EnhancedSessionStore.php:2083-2103`) then runs `clearAll()` plus a per-session `syncMessages()` with no enclosing transaction: one WAL commit per row, run inline from `listSessionsFiltered()` (`:962`) on `update()`. The review measured 128 s at 300 sessions. Any throw inside `search()` also sets `dirty`, which forces another full rebuild.
- **Fix, three parts:**
1. Run the sweep inside `sessionStore->immediateTransaction()`, chunked at about 500 sessions per transaction so a concurrent writer can interleave.
2. Persist the build state in a `session_search_meta(version, built_at, dirty)` row written in the same transaction. `needsRebuild()` becomes "no marker, a version mismatch, or a recorded dirty flag", and a failed sync records `dirty = 1` durably. The incremental `syncSearchIndex()` already keeps a built index current across processes.
3. In `search()`, treat `SQLITE_BUSY`/`SQLITE_LOCKED` as "cannot answer now": return `null` (the LIKE degrade) and do not mark the index dirty.
- **What the user sees:** the first `/sessions <q>` stops freezing on every launch. Only the first build per database costs anything, and that build runs in one transaction.
C-SES-2.a.files.modify: `candy-code/src/Session/SessionSearchIndex.php` (createSchema, needsRebuild, markBuilt, syncMessages catch, search catch), `candy-code/src/Session/EnhancedSessionStore.php` (rebuildSearchIndex())
C-SES-2.a.risks: Old databases have no marker and rebuild once, after which they are trusted. The marker must also be cleared by `clearAll()` and `collectGarbage()` failure paths.

C-SES-2.b.title: Picker shows body hits + snippets + per-row spend; `/` filter reaches FTS
C-SES-2.b.item: C-SES-2 (+ C-SES-1's SES-1-P4 picker half) (sources: SES-2-P1, p2-miss: picker body snippet (`SessionRow::withBodySnippet` dormant), SES-1-P4, p2-miss: per-session spend on picker)
C-SES-2.b.approach:
- **Root cause.** `buildSessionPicker()` (`src/Chat.php:14668-14689`) fetches FTS-ranked rows through `sessionPickerRows()` (`:14714-14733`), then calls `withQuery()`. `SessionPicker::rankedLayout()` (`src/Tui/SessionPicker.php:349-374`) keeps only rows whose `haystack()` (`:376-385`: title, summary, agent, id, branch) passes a `requireFullQuery` Smith-Waterman match, so a body-only hit is dropped. The Ctrl+R `/` filter reads the store once, when it opens (`Chat.php:14963-14969`: "typing a query never touches the store").
- **Fix, in the rows.** `sanitizeSessionRows()` carries two new keys:
- `bodySnippet`, from `SessionRow::$bodySnippet` (`:53`, `:106`), sanitized like the other fields;
- `spend`, as `SpendLedger::boundUsd(costUnpriced, costUsd)` when `costUsd !== null`. This wires the write-only cache (SES-1-P4).
- **Fix, in the picker.**
- `rankedLayout()` admits store-ranked rows (a non-null `bodySnippet`) after the fuzzy hits, in bm25 order.
- `renderRow()` paints the snippet as a faint second line under body-matched rows, and the spend in the meta column.
- In filter mode, the picker emits `SessionListAction::Filter` on every query edit.
- **Fix, in Chat.** Chat debounces those edits: a 300 ms Cmd tick returns `SessionPickerSearchMsg(query)`. When it arrives, Chat re-reads `sessionPickerRows(SEARCH_LIMIT, archived, query)` only if the picker's query still matches.
- **What the user sees:**
- `/sessions anchor` lists a session that matched only in its body, with the snippet;
- typing in Ctrl+R reaches the full-text index;
- each row shows its spend.
C-SES-2.b.files.modify: `candy-code/src/Chat.php` (buildSessionPicker, sanitizeSessionRows, runSessionListAction: Filter arm), `candy-code/src/Chat/Handlers/HandlesSessionSurface.php` (the SessionPickerSearchMsg arm), `candy-code/src/Tui/SessionPicker.php` (rankedLayout, haystack, renderRow, filter-key emission)
C-SES-2.b.tests:
create `candy-code/tests/Chat/SessionPickerDebouncedSearchTest.php`: a stale query is ignored and a fresh one re-reads the store. Modify:
- `candy-code/tests/Chat/SessionCommandTest.php`: the VISIBLE rows of `/sessions anchor` include the body-only session. This replaces the reflection pin on the private page read, which asserts the wrong layer.
- `candy-code/tests/Tui/SessionPickerFilterTest.php`: store-ranked rows are admitted; the LIKE degrade keeps its polarity.
- `candy-code/tests/Tui/SessionPickerSlashFilterTest.php`: query edits emit `Filter`.
- `candy-code/tests/Tui/SessionPickerGoldenTest.php`: re-pin the goldens with snippet and spend.
C-SES-2.b.docs/guards: none (no new key binding, since `/` already exists)
C-SES-2.b.risks: P-SESSION-TABS also touches the session-switch and picker surfaces. Do not run them in the same wave.

C-SES-2.c.title: Protocol: summaries carry snippets + honest spend; web body search + live `≥`
C-SES-2.c.item: C-SES-2 (+ C-SES-1's web half) (sources: GAP-SES-11, SES-1-P2, SES-1-P4, p2-miss: per-session spend on sidebar)
C-SES-2.c.approach:
- **Root cause (web search).** `SessionMethods::list()` filters `query` by `str_contains` over name, id and `last_preview` (`src/Protocol/Methods/SessionMethods.php:82-113`). It never reaches FTS.
- **Root cause (spend).** The `D::USAGE` wire schema omits `unpricedModel` (`src/Protocol/Schema/Definitions.php:185-193`), although `UsageUpdated` sends it. The reducer sets `unpriced` only from the snapshot (`candy-code-web/src-web/stores/reducer.ts:271`), so a live unpriced turn reads `$0.00`. `SessionSummary.spentUsd` exists only for open hosts (`src/Protocol/ServerContext.php:337`).
- **Fix, server.**
- `SessionHub::list()` gains `?string $query`, which runs `EnhancedSessionStore::listSessionsFiltered(SessionQuery::new()->withBodySearch($q))`: FTS-ranked, with the LIKE degrade.
- `SessionMethods::list()` delegates to it.
- `ServerContext::summary()` adds three fields: `snippet`; `spentUsd`, falling back to the row's `cost_usd` for closed sessions; and `spendUnpriced`, from the row's `cost_unpriced`. The cache is updated in the ledger's own transaction.
- `D::USAGE` gains `unpricedModel` (nullable string), and `SESSION_SUMMARY` gains `snippet` and `spendUnpriced`. Then regenerate the chain.
- **Fix, web.**
- The reducer's `usage.updated` arm sets `state.unpriced = true` when `turnUsage.unpricedModel` is non-empty.
- `sessions.ts` gains a `search(query)` that calls `session.list {query}`, debounced 250 ms.
- `SessionSidebar.vue` routes its filter to the server and paints the snippet plus `spendLabel(s.spentUsd, s.spendUnpriced)` per row.
C-SES-2.c.files.modify: `candy-code/src/Protocol/Methods/SessionMethods.php` (list()), `candy-code/src/Host/SessionHub.php` (list()), `candy-code/src/Protocol/ServerContext.php` (summary()), `candy-code/src/Protocol/Schema/Definitions.php` (SESSION_SUMMARY, USAGE), `candy-code/docs/protocol/candy-code.v1.schema.json` (regen), `candy-code/docs/SERVER.md` (regen), `candy-code-web/src-web/protocol/generated.ts` (regen), `candy-code-web/src-web/stores/reducer.ts` (usage.updated arm), `candy-code-web/src-web/stores/sessions.ts` (search), `candy-code-web/src-web/components/SessionSidebar.vue` (filter → server search; row snippet + spend)
C-SES-2.c.docs/guards:
the generation chain:
1. `php candy-code/scripts/gen-protocol-schema.php` regenerates the schema JSON and `docs/SERVER.md`;
2. `npm run gen:protocol` regenerates `generated.ts`.

Guards moved: `ProtocolSchemaDriftTest`, `ServerProtocolDocumentationDriftTest`, `generated.spec.ts`.
C-SES-2.c.risks: `SessionHub::list()` pages arrays while the FTS path returns `SessionRow` objects. Convert through `SessionRow::toArray()` and keep cursor paging stable.

C-SES-3.a.title: Shares die with their session; token redacted from the serve log
C-SES-3.a.approach:
- **Root cause.** `shares` has no FK to `sessions` (`src/Share/ShareStore.php:54-62`), and no delete or prune path touches it. `SessionStore::deleteSessionTrees()` (`src/Session/SessionStore.php:1005-1052`) is the single choke that both `deleteSession()` (`:992`) and `pruneSessions()` (`:1267ff`) use. A deleted or pruned session therefore keeps `/s/<token>` live for up to 365 days, and nothing can list the token.
- **Root cause (log).** Separately, `Server.php:226-229` logs `getUri()->getPath()`, which includes the 32-hex capability token.
- **Fix.**
- Inside `deleteSessionTrees()`'s existing transaction, run a chunked `UPDATE shares SET revoked_at = ? WHERE revoked_at IS NULL AND session_id IN (…)`. Guard it with `hasTable('shares')`, since `shares` sits in the same `session.db`. The SQL lives once, as a `ShareStore` public constant or static helper.
- Add `ShareStore::liveAll()`: every live share across sessions, LEFT JOIN `sessions` for the name, with orphans flagged.
- The access-log closure redacts `/s/<token>` to `/s/<first 4 hex>…`, keyed on `ShareStore::URL_PREFIX`.
C-SES-3.a.files.modify: `candy-code/src/Session/SessionStore.php` (deleteSessionTrees()), `candy-code/src/Share/ShareStore.php` (liveAll(), the revoke-for-sessions SQL), `candy-code/src/Server/Server.php` (the access-log middleware closure)
C-SES-3.a.risks: Revoke rather than delete, so the row stays listable as revoked and auditable. `sweepInertRows()` later reaps it.

C-SES-3.b.title: `/share list` across sessions; revoke hardening
C-SES-3.b.item: C-SES-3 (+ C-SES-9's SES-3-P3) (sources: SES-3-P1, SES-3-P3, p2-miss: cross-session `/share list`)
C-SES-3.b.approach:
- **`/share list`.** New subcommand: render `ShareStore::liveAll()` as token prefix, session name (or "deleted session"), expiry and format. `/share revoke` with no token now lists every live share, not just `liveForSession(currentSessionId)` (`src/Commands/ShareCommand.php:228`).
- **SES-3-P3.**
- `ShareHostCommand` wraps `ob_start()…execute()` in `try/finally { ob_get_clean() }`.
- `ShareCommand::revoke()` catches `RuntimeException`/`PDOException` from `shareStoreFor()` (`:258-269`) and `ShareStore::revoke()`, the same way `serve()` already does.
- **Hint.** `cmd.share.hint` gains `list`. The hint is a Lang key, so `0400-share.php` is not edited.
C-SES-3.b.tests: create `candy-code/tests/Host/ShareHostCommandBufferTest.php`: a read-only database gives a failure result and `ob_get_level()` is unchanged. Modify `candy-code/tests/Commands/ShareCommandTest.php`: the list includes other sessions' and deleted sessions' shares; bare revoke lists everything.

C-SES-3.c.title: `session.shares` read RPC (for C-WEB-3's menu)
C-SES-3.c.item: C-SES-3 (sources: p2-miss: `session.shares` RPC + web share UI, SES-3-P4)
C-SES-3.c.approach: Add `session.shares {sessionId?}`, Scope Read. It returns the live shares of one session, or of every session when `sessionId` is absent. Each row carries a token prefix, the full token (the method is token-scoped, the same as `session.share`'s answer), path, expiry, format and session name. C-WEB-3's Share/Revoke menu consumes it alongside the existing `session.share` and `session.unshare`.
C-SES-3.c.tests: modify `candy-code/tests/Protocol/ShareMethodsTest.php`: per-session and all-sessions listings, and a revoked share leaves the list.
